questions.title: Retrieve all information on all of the books
questions.description: Return every document in the book collection.
questions.referenceNotes: db.collection.find({}) with no filter returns everything.

questions.title: Books written by Danielle Steel
questions.description:
Retrieve the title of every book where an author's first name is 'Danielle'.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: Dot notation reaches into an array of embedded documents: 'author.firstname'. Suppress _id with a projection.

questions.title: Users living in Boston
questions.description:
Retrieve the username of every user who has an address in the city 'Boston'.

Return only the field: username.
questions.referenceNotes: address is an array of objects, so 'address.city' matches if any element matches.

questions.title: Books with multiple publishers
questions.description:
List the title of every book that has more than one publisher.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: A second array element exists when 'publisher.1' exists, or use $size in an $expr.

questions.title: Books that have notes
questions.description:
List the title of every book whose notes array is not empty.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: An empty array is not the same as a missing field. $ne: [] or $size work here.

questions.title: Books published by Indian publishers
questions.description:
Find the title of every book that has at least one publisher whose address country is 'India'.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: publisher is an array and each element has an embedded address object.

testCases.label: Four Indian-published books
testCases.expectedOutput: [{"title": "Computer Networks"}, {"title": "Database Concepts"}, {"title": "Operating System Concepts"}, {"title": "Tamil Ilakkiya Varalaru"}]

questions.title: Books published by more than two publishers
questions.description:
List the title of every book with more than two publishers.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: Compare $size against a number inside $expr, or use an aggregation $match.

questions.title: Count of books currently available
questions.description: Return the number of books whose available field is 'Y', as a single value.
questions.referenceNotes: countDocuments returns a plain number, which this platform shows in a column named value.

questions.title: Language-wise book count
questions.description:
Group the books by their language and return the number of books in each.

Return the fields: language, count.
questions.referenceNotes: $group with _id: '$language' and $sum: 1, then $project to rename _id to language.

questions.title: Top two publishers by number of books
questions.description:
Count how many books each publisher has published, then return the top two.

Return the fields: publisher, books. Break ties by publisher name ascending.
questions.referenceNotes: $unwind the publisher array first, then $group, $sort, $limit.

testCases.label: Two publishers with two books each

questions.title: Second author of every multi-author book
questions.description:
For each book that has at least two authors, print the book title and the second author's first and last name.

Return the fields: title, firstname, lastname.
questions.referenceNotes: $arrayElemAt with index 1 picks the second element of an array.

questions.title: Aggregation pipeline: books published from Chennai
questions.description:
Write an aggregation pipeline that returns the book title and the first author's first name for every book published by a publisher in the city 'Chennai', ordered by book title.

Return the fields: title, author_firstname.
questions.referenceNotes: $unwind, then $match on publisher.city, then $project and $sort. This question checks the order of your rows.

testCases.label: Ordered by title
testCases.expectedOutput: [{"title": "Computer Networks", "author_firstname": "Andrew"}, {"title": "Database Concepts", "author_firstname": "Abraham"}, {"title": "Operating System Concepts", "author_firstname": "Abraham"}, {"title": "Tamil Ilakkiya Varalaru", "author_firstname": "Mu"}]

questions.title: Books borrowed by the user 'ram' ($lookup)
questions.description:
Using $lookup to join book.user against user.mobileno, print the titles of the books borrowed by the user whose username is 'ram'.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: $lookup is a left outer join. Unwind the joined array before matching on the username.

questions.title: Books left with no notes
questions.description:
Find the title of every book whose notes array is empty.

Return only the field: title.
questions.referenceNotes: The opposite of the earlier notes question. $size: 0 matches an empty array.

questions.title: Explain your aggregation approach
questions.description:
In comments at the top of your script, explain in four or five sentences why $unwind was needed for the publisher questions but not for the simple find() queries, and what would change if a book could have no publisher at all.

Then print your roll number.
questions.referenceNotes: This question is read by your teacher. There are no test cases.

worksheets.title: Lab Exercise 2 - Object Relational Database
worksheets.description: Structured types, collections and nested access, run on PostgreSQL. The composite types ADDRESS_TY and PERSON_TY and the table CUSTOMER_1 are already created for you. The Oracle-only features - VARRAY, nested tables, REF and type inheritance - are in the separate Oracle worksheet, which needs the department server.

questions.title: Print all customer details
questions.description:
Print the customer id, first name, last name and city of every customer in CUSTOMER_1, ordered by customer id.

Return the columns: customer_id, firstname, lastname, city.
questions.referenceNotes: The person column is a composite type. Reach into it with (person).firstname, and nest further with (person).addr.city. The parentheses are required.

questions.title: Street of a specific customer
questions.description:
Fetch the street of the customer whose customer_id is 3.

Return the column: street.
questions.referenceNotes: Two levels of composite access: (person).addr.street.

questions.title: Total phone contacts per customer
questions.description:
Get the number of phone contacts held for each customer.

Return the columns: customer_id, phone_count. A customer with no phones must still appear, with a count of 0.
questions.referenceNotes: phones is an array column. array_length(phones, 1) returns NULL for an empty array, so wrap it in coalesce(..., 0).

questions.title: Customers living in Tamilnadu
questions.description:
Print the first name and age of every customer whose state is 'Tamilnadu'.

Return the columns: firstname, age.
questions.referenceNotes: Filter on the nested composite field in the WHERE clause.

questions.title: Create your own object table and insert into it
questions.description:
Create a table named CUSTOMER_2 with the columns (customer_id integer, person person_ty) and insert at least 3 rows into it, using the person_ty and address_ty types that already exist.

Your script is checked by counting the rows you inserted.
questions.referenceNotes: Construct a composite value with ROW(...)::person_ty. The verification query runs after your script, so create the table and insert in one go.

testCases.label: At least three rows inserted
testCases.input: SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) >= 3 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'too few' END AS result FROM customer_2;

questions.title: Why object-relational?
questions.description:
In comments at the top of your script, explain in four or five sentences what the composite type bought you over three plain columns, and one thing Oracle's VARRAY and nested tables give you that the array column here does not.

Then select your roll number as a single column named roll.
questions.referenceNotes: Read by your teacher. No test cases.

worksheets.title: Lab Exercise 3 - Oracle Object Types, VARRAY and REF
worksheets.description: The Oracle-specific half of the object-relational syllabus: CREATE TYPE ... AS OBJECT, VARRAY, nested tables, REF and type inheritance. This worksheet runs against the department's Oracle server, so it stays a draft until ORACLE_CONNECT_STRING is configured on the platform.

questions.title: Create ADDRESS_TY and PERSON_TY object types
questions.description:
Create an object type ADDRESS_TY with Street, City, State and Zip, and an object type PERSON_TY with Name and an ADDRESS_TY attribute. Then create a table CUSTOMER with Customer_ID and a PERSON_TY column, and insert one row.

Your script is checked by counting the rows in CUSTOMER.
questions.referenceNotes: create or replace type ADDRESS_TY as object (...); terminate each type with a / on its own line, as in SQL*Plus.

testCases.label: One customer inserted
testCases.input: SELECT count(*) AS c FROM CUSTOMER

questions.title: Varying array of tools
questions.description:
Create a VARRAY type TOOLS_VA holding up to 5 VARCHAR2(25) values, a table BORROWER(Name, Tools), and insert the borrower 'JED HOPKINS' with the tools HAMMER, SLEDGE and AX.

Your script is checked by unnesting the array.
questions.referenceNotes: select B.Name, N.* from BORROWER B, TABLE(B.Tools) N;

testCases.label: Three tools stored
testCases.input: SELECT count(*) AS c FROM BORROWER B, TABLE(B.Tools) N

questions.title: Doctor and patient with REF and type inheritance
questions.description:
Design object types for a doctor and a patient so that a patient holds a REF to their doctor, and a specialist doctor type inherits from the base doctor type using UNDER. Insert enough data to answer: find the doctor name and contact information of the patient 'Siddarth'.

This question is read by your teacher.
questions.referenceNotes: create type SPECIALIST_TY under DOCTOR_TY (...). Use DEREF to follow a REF.

worksheets.title: Lab Exercise 1 - Arrays, Strings and Sorting
worksheets.description: Warm-up exercises in C, C++, Java and Python. Each program reads from standard input and prints to standard output exactly as the test cases show.

questions.title: Sum of two integers
questions.description: Read two integers separated by whitespace and print their sum on one line.
questions.referenceNotes: C: scanf("%d %d", &a, &b). Python: map(int, input().split()).

questions.title: Reverse an array
questions.description: The first line of input is n. The second line has n space-separated integers. Print them in reverse order, space separated, on one line.
questions.referenceNotes: Print a single space between values and a newline at the end, with no trailing space.

questions.title: Count vowels in a string
questions.description: Read one line of text and print the number of vowels in it. Count both upper and lower case a, e, i, o, u.
questions.referenceNotes: Read the whole line, including spaces. In C, fgets is safer than scanf("%s").

questions.title: Explain your sorting choice
questions.description: In a comment at the top of your program, explain in three or four sentences which sorting algorithm you would use to sort one lakh integers and why. Then print your roll number on a single line.
questions.referenceNotes: Graded by your teacher, not by test cases.
